chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Saeed al-Naqqash, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, in Al-Fitr there is Takbeer, but it is concealed.' I said, 'And where is it?' He said: 'On the night of Al-Fitr, during Maghrib and the last Isha, and in the Fajr prayer, and in the Eid prayer. Then it is cut off.'

I said, 'How should I say it?' He said: 'You should say: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, There is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs the praise, Allah is the Greatest for what He guided us.' And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to make complete the period [of fasting] and to magnify Allah for that He has guided you.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf ibn Hammad — similar to it.

key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)
key_terms.تَكْبِيراً: Takbeer (Exalming Allah by saying 'Allah is the Greatest')
key_terms.مَسْتُورٌ: Concealed (referring to reciting quietly or individually rather than aloud in congregation)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific time and formula for reciting Takbeer on the night of Eid al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific protocol for the concealed Takbeer during the night and day of Eid al-Fitr, emphasizing its recitation during Maghrib, Isha, Fajr, and the Eid prayer itself. It provides the precise formula—'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illa Allahu, wa Allahu Akbar, wa lillahi al-hamd'—and explicitly links it to the Quranic command to magnify Allah for guidance, reinforcing the Shia practice of integrating liturgical praise with scriptural injunctions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Saeed Al Naqqash who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘In Al-Fitr (1<sup>st</sup> of Shawwal), there is a Takbeer (exclamations of the Greatness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>), but it is concealed. I said, ‘And where is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The night of Al-Fits during Al-Maghrib and Al-Isha the last, and in Al-Fajr Prayer, and in the Eid Prayer. Then it is cut-off’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘How should I be saying?’ Heasws said: ‘You should be saying, ‘Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description)! Allahazwj is the Greatest(beyond description)! There is no god except for Allahazwj and Allahazwj is the Greatest! Allahazwj is the Greatest and for Allahazwj is the Praise upon what Heazwj Guided us’, and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:185] and (He Desires) that you should complete the number - Meaning the Fasts - and that you should exclaim the Greatness of Allah for His having Guided you’.
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Khalaf Bin Hammad – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Khalaf ibn Hammad from Sa‘id al-Naqqash who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘On al-Fitr (first day of the month of Shawwal), there is Takbir (saying ‘Allah is great beyond description’), and it is Mastur (masnun) optional.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘Where is it?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is during the night of al-Fitr, in Maghrib and ‘Isha’, in salat (prayer) and in salat (prayer) of ‘Id, and then it is discontinued.’

I (the narrator) then asked, ‘How do I say it?’ He (the Imam) replied, say, ‘Allah is great beyond description, Allah is great beyond description, only Allah deserves worship, Allah is great beyond description, Allah is great beyond description, All praise belongs to Allah, Allah is great beyond description; He has granted us guidance. This is in the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, “So you can complete the number (fasting)’, [2:182] and say, ‘Allah is great beyond description; He had granted you guidance.”””
NOTE: A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Khalaf ibn Hammad a similar Hadith.
